why: Both rows state the Houthis' ban on the Aden central bank's new notes, a rule an authority sets: 'In Ansar Allah-controlled areas, where the newly printed IRG banknotes were banned in 2020' (YQ-D220, YE-D239) and 'the new currency banned, and liable to be confiscated or torn if found on travellers' (YQ-E620, YE-E696). Yet they sit at Houthi-controlled areas, a second part of today on the same ground, while step 2b placed the same ban's other rows from that area at Houthis' area (YQ-D037, YQ-E287, YQ-E621, YQ-D077).
fix: Place YQ-D220 and YQ-E620 at Houthis' area.

why: 'coins circulating in everyday trade' (YQ-E317: 50- and 100-rial coins 'circulating mainly outside the banking sector, in everyday commercial transactions') and 'Aden's 200-rial note refused by exchange companies' (YQ-E605, an economist) report what circulates or is accepted in practice, not whether the coins and notes may be used, which the group's other rows state as rules. The review round split the same two questions for prints (YG-568 from YG-024).
fix: Move YQ-E317 and YQ-E605 to a condition on whether a central bank's new coins and notes circulate or are accepted in practice.

why: 'eight banks decided to move to Aden' (YQ-D492, YQ-D001, and at place not stated YQ-C383, YQ-E339, YQ-E526) and YQ-D493's 'Sana'a banks moving to Aden' ('several Yemeni banks headquartered in Sanaa decided to relocate their operations to Aden') state the March 2025 decision with and without its count and list. They carry two labels and tie on 15 March 2025 at Sana'a and Aden.
fix: One label for these rows (the banks' decision to move to Aden), with the count and the banks named in note.

why: 'US dollar correspondent accounts closed' (YQ-D437: in 2015 to 2019, 'the closure of Yemeni banks' U.S. dollar accounts with correspondent banks', YE-D623) states, at more detail, the isolation that 'Severely restricted' states for 2017 and 2020 (YQ-E285, YQ-E313). So 2019 reads as a change between them.
fix: Label YQ-D437 'Severely restricted', with the dollar accounts in note.

why: Item 006 (15 December 2025) states two facts side by side: transfers 'restricted, tied to one specified network, with strict ceilings' after the Houthis' decision (YQ-D028, YE-D030), and the ban on dealing with the Aden central bank's unified network ('منع التعامل مع الشبكة الموحدة', YQ-D029, YE-D031). They hold together, and they show as two parts of today only because one sits at Houthi-controlled areas and the other at Houthis' area.
fix: Move YQ-D028 to its own condition (whether transfers in the Houthis' areas are tied to one specified network, with ceilings), by the brief's parts of one source.

why: 'First phase launched with seven banks' (YQ-C390) reports the national switch ('نظام المقسم الوطني', YE-C396), not the unified network ('الشبكة الموحدة') that the condition names, and the same item reports the two apart (YQ-C389, YE-C395). Named for one network, the condition takes another network's members, and today shows them at Central Bank of Yemen's area beside the unified network's own members at two other places.
fix: Name the condition at the act (which banks, exchange companies and e-wallets are linked to a money transfer network), with each network's service as the place: the unified network's for YQ-C389, YQ-D475 and YQ-D279, and the national switch's for YQ-C390. Or move YQ-C390 to its own condition.

why: 'Up 300%' (YQ-D627: commissions that 'زادت بنسبة 300٪', rose by 300 percent, YE-D986) states the rise that 'Increased' (YQ-D478, YQ-E832) states, with its figure. The two labels make the group an axis, though no row states a change.
fix: Label YQ-D627 'Increased', with its 300 percent in note.

why: 'About 800 unlicensed, beside 550 licensed' (YQ-D356, 2017) and 'About 800 of 1,350 unlicensed' (YQ-D211, YQ-D428, 2018: 'nearly 800 of the 1,350 money exchange outlets and companies') state the same count, about 800 unlicensed and 550 licensed. They carry two labels, so 2018 reads as a change from 2017.
fix: One label for rows YQ-D356, YQ-D211 and YQ-D428, with the licensed count and its fall from 605 in note.

why: 'Available at registered merchants' (YQ-E207: customers can 'purchase goods from registered merchants', YE-E211) states the availability that every other row's 'Available' states, with where. It is the axis's only other label, so the group holds no change.
fix: Label YQ-E207 'Available', with registered merchants in note.

why: Four partial lists hold together at place not stated: the Post's E-Rial with Rial Mobile in trial (YQ-B057, 2018), a guide's five wallets (YQ-E750, May 2025), 'banks including Tadhamon, YKB, YCB, IBY, CAC, Shamil, Al-Amal and Kuraimi offer wallets' (YQ-D094, June 2025) and a tracker's 16 apps (YQ-F069, August 2026). None gives the whole list. Yet the latest replaces the others in today, and each earlier list builds a case as if it were the set of wallets. My first review's fix put them together.
fix: Give each source's list its own condition, named by its source, as the brief's lists that grow does. Or give these rows one label, with each list in note.

why: At place not stated, lists that hold together replace one another: Mahfathati's and PYes's services (YQ-D522, October 2022), 'Purchases and bills, among others' (YQ-D091, YQ-D092, June 2025) and 'The notification types a community tracker covers for four wallets' (YQ-F070, August 2026). Today gives the last as what a phone wallet offers.
fix: One label for these rows, 'Transfers, purchases and bills, among others' as at the services, with each list in note, as the fix did for each wallet's pages.

why: SabaCash's 'a discount for a limited period' (YQ-C317: 'كاش باك على مشترياته', cashback on purchases, offered 'لفترة محدودة', for a limited period) and Hasseb's 'discounts or cashback at named merchants' state the same offer: one gives how long it runs, the other where. They are the axis's only two labels, so the group holds no change.
fix: One label for these rows (discounts or cashback offered), with where and how long in note.

why: Item 153 gives the non-bank and bank-led models as 'two separate models emerging from the two competing central bank branches' (YE-E126), rules the two central banks set. Yet YQ-E115 and YQ-E116 sit at the areas the text names, while item 154's account of the same two models sits at Houthis' area and the IRG's area (YQ-E152, YQ-E153). Placed there, YQ-E116 (September 2025) would make 'banks only' today at the IRG's area, in place of 'banks and licensed non-bank institutions' (August 2023), a disagreement between sources that the current places hide.
fix: Place YQ-E115 at Houthis' area and YQ-E116 at the internationally recognized government's area.

why: Three rows give a rate at one time, not an average over a stated period. YQ-D187 is the average of Aden dealers' quotes on one page ('متوسط أسعار صرف الدولار في عدن', YE-D203), which my first review wrongly listed among the period averages. YQ-E447 is 'an average of YR539 per US$1 at the beginning of July compared to YR532 on June 25' (YE-E469). YQ-E392 is 'from YR1,630 to YR1,573 per US$1 on average' toward the end of February, a price then 'maintained' (YE-E409).
fix: Move YQ-D187, YQ-E447 and YQ-E392 back to the rial's market price (YG-001).

why: 'remittances the Houthi group controls' (YQ-D465: 'most incoming foreign currency remittances, which the Houthi group controlled to fund imports') and 'remittances from Yemenis abroad' (YQ-E727) state the same origin, and the first adds who controls it. They are the axis's only two labels, so the group holds no change.
fix: One label for rows YQ-D465 and YQ-E727 (remittances from abroad), with the Houthi group's control in note.

why: Item 155 uses 'the south' and 'government-controlled areas' for the same area, the one where the Aden central bank's notes circulate. The notes 'now circulate in the south following a ban by Houthi authorities' (YE-E266), and they 'soon flooded into government-controlled areas' (YE-E296). Yet 'the south' stands alone, so 'new notes in use' is a second part of today on the same ground.
fix: Group place 'the south' with 'government-controlled areas' (why: source; basis: YE-E266, YE-E296).

why: 'old notes mainly in use' (YQ-E180) reads item 154's 'old rial banknotes, used primarily in Houthi-controlled northern areas' (YE-E185), where 'primarily' says where the old notes are used. So it states what 'old notes in use' states (YQ-E258, YQ-C458), and 2026 reads as a change from 2022.
fix: Label YQ-E180 'old notes in use'.

why: Three different measures and lists hold together: costs by provider (YQ-E817: 'Fawri the lowest at 2.07 percent; MoneyGram 3.90 and Western Union 4.41 percent', June 2024), costs by channel (YQ-D304: '5-8% through traditional banks', '5-12% through informal remittance offices', April 2025), and the fees surveyed migrants paid (YQ-E815: 'fees of USD 1-5 (29 respondents) and USD 6-10 (13)', February 2026). Yet the survey replaces the others in today. My first review's fix put them together.
fix: Move the survey's fees (YQ-E815) to their own condition. Give YQ-E817's providers and YQ-D304's channels each their own condition, or one label with each list in note.

why: 'low' (YQ-E223) is the label this row had in YG-511, on how widely wallets are used. Here it names no use, though its source names them: e-rials 'restricted to financial transfers among held accounts, capped cash-in or cash-out transactions, and to a minimal extent the payment of cell phone, internet, electricity, and water bills' (YE-E228). So today gives 'low' as what buyers use wallets for.
fix: Label YQ-E223 with the uses it names (transfers between accounts, capped cash in and out, and few bills).

why: The Cash wallet's pages state different facts, which hold together. One gives withdrawals 'عبر وكلاء الخدمة' (through service agents) 'في أي وقت من اوقات الدوام الرسمي' (during official working hours) (YQ-C127, YE-C110). The other gives 'سيولة نقدية متوفرة على مدار الساعة' (cash available around the clock) (YQ-C178, YE-C155), which Cash's English page explains as cash-out 'through Automatic Teller Machine (ATM) during off work times' (YE-E774). So no source makes today's 'disputed @ Cash e-wallet's service'.
fix: Give YQ-C178 its own condition (whether the wallet's cash is available around the clock), by the brief's parts of one source, so that YQ-C127 states the agents' hours alone.

why: Each article of 11 July 2026 gives both figures side by side and sets neither against the other. Item 076 counts 'ما بين 8 و10' wallets (YE-C471), then gives 'نحو 9 محافظ تعد الأشهر والأكثر انتشارا، وقد يصل العدد إلى أكثر من 15' (YE-C474). Item 077 gives 'ما بين ثماني وعشر' (YE-C488), and says the number 'قد يتجاوز 15' (YE-C489). The wallets in view (8 to 10, about 9 best known) and a possible total (over 15) hold together, so no source makes today's 'disputed @ place not stated'.
fix: One label for YQ-C444, YQ-C445 and YQ-C461 (8 to 10, as 'about 9' is the same count at different detail), with 'may exceed 15' in note. YQ-C462, which gives the possible total alone, goes to its own condition, or takes the same label as the articles' hedge on that count.

why: 'none, up to 3,000,000 rials' (YQ-E044, YQ-E063: 'you can transfer up to 3,000,000 Yemeni Riyals to any ONE Cash subscriber, no commission at all', YE-E067) states the 'none' of YQ-C367, together with ONE Cash's transfer ceiling, which does not limit the free fee. They are the axis's only two labels, so the group holds no change.
fix: Label YQ-E044 and YQ-E063 'none', with the 3,000,000-rial ceiling in note.
